name: The Bellows Intercept
image_style: A layered fresco-secco and powdered graphite illustration on warm lime plaster, combining matte mineral pigment, hairline architectural drafting, rubbed charcoal haze, and occasional translucent shellac glints on metal. The mood is chivalric, industrial, nocturnal, and gently absurd: a historically grounded medieval siege workshop treated with complete seriousness while an unmistakable cosmic visitor performs the wrong job with heroic concentration. Use a rare palette of furnace-black, bruised blue, chalked apricot, tarnished green-bronze, bone white, and tiny sparks of arterial red. Build broad smoky negative space across the quiet upper edge and leave a calm dark region near the left side for widgets; concentrate tactile detail in the lower-right machinery and figures. No lettering, logos, borders, frames, UI, watermarks, sacred parody, or devotional attributes.
scene: Exactly one striking 16:10 landscape desktop wallpaper, preferably 2560x1600, set inside a historically grounded medieval siege-engine workshop at night beneath an open timber shed beside a walled European town. Massive timber beams, rope coils, oak wheels, iron fittings, stacked counterweights, tool racks, charcoal braziers, and a half-built trebuchet are rendered with practical historical accuracy. In the lower-right, Space Ghost is unmistakable in his muscular white costume, black hood and mask, yellow cape, and red power bands, solemnly working an enormous hand bellows with one gloved hand while holding a tiny surveyor's plumb line in the other, as though certifying the machine's engineering. His cape is pinned safely away from the coals. Tired craftsmen continue their dignified work around him with restrained bewilderment; a patient draft horse watches from shadow. The humor comes only from his misplaced technical confidence and impossible scale. Keep the broad upper sky and roofline dark, sparse, and quiet for a desktop panel, with a calm widget-friendly shadow on the left. No sacred figures, worship, halos, devotional objects, text, lettering, logos, interface elements, watermark, or frame.
